meta.description: The official API for TAIRED CBT question bank.

data.question: What is a system?
data.a: A single component that works alone
data.b: An organized collection of components that work together to achieve a specific goal
data.c: A random set of unrelated parts
data.d: A type of computer software only

data.question: What are inputs?
data.b: The resources, data, or materials put into a system to be processed
data.c: The mechanisms that monitor system operation
data.d: The limits that define the system

data.question: What is feedback?
data.a: The final product of the system
data.b: Information about output used to make adjustments to inputs or processes
data.c: The physical devices used in the system
data.d: The external factors that influence the system

data.question: An information system is specifically designed to:
data.b: Manage and process data to provide useful information for decision-making

data.question: What are the four fundamental phases of the SDLC?
data.b: Planning, analysis, design, implementation

data.question: What does a feasibility analysis examine?
data.a: Only the cost of the project
data.b: Technical feasibility, economic feasibility, and organizational feasibility

data.question: When are projects typically identified in an organization?
data.a: When a random idea is suggested by external stakeholders
data.b: When someone in the organization identifies a business need to build a system
data.c: When the organization wants to test new computer hardware
data.d: When the development team finishes all their current tasks

data.question: Which of the following is considered a business need that might trigger a project?
data.a: Routine maintenance of existing software applications
data.b: Responding to pain points like a drop in market share or poor customer service

data.question: What is the definition of emerging technology?
data.a: Technology that is universally accepted and used in all modern businesses
data.b: Technology that is still being developed and not yet viable for widespread business use
data.c: Technology that has become obsolete and needs replacement
data.d: Standard computer hardware components used for data entry

data.question: Which of the following examples are given as emerging technologies?
data.a: Local Area Networks and desktop computers
data.b: Cloud computing, RFID, and Web 2.0
data.c: Standard operating systems and enterprise applications
data.d: Customer records and sales transactions databases

data.question: How is a project typically identified?
data.a: The systems analyst chooses any project they desire
data.b: Someone in the organization identifies a business need to build a system
data.c: The IT department randomly selects a project
data.d: An external consultant always initiates the project

data.question: Which of the following is an example of a business need?
data.b: Supporting a new marketing campaign

data.question: What is emerging technology?
data.b: Technology that is still being developed and not yet viable for widespread business use
data.c: Technology that every company already uses
data.d: Technology that only governments can access

data.question: What does BPM stand for?
data.b: Basic Program Memory

data.question: What is Business Process Management (BPM)?
data.a: A methodology to eliminate all business processes
data.b: A methodology used to continuously improve end-to-end business processes

data.question: Which feasibility analysis asks the question "will it work when deployed"?
data.b: Economic Feasibility

data.question: Which development methodology uses a sequential approach where each phase completes before the next begins?
data.b: Waterfall development

data.question: Who evaluates projects in the context of a portfolio balancing risks and returns?
data.b: The IT Department

data.question: Which element of a system request document describes the constraints relevant to implementation?
data.b: Special Issues

data.question: Which of the following is NOT typically a factor that influences methodology selection?
data.b: Reliability needs

data.question: What does the term analysis mean in systems analysis?
data.b: Breaking a whole into its parts to understand their nature, function, and interrelationships
data.c: Testing a system after it is built

data.question: What are the three steps of the basic process of analysis?
data.b: Understand as-is system, identify improvements, define requirements for to-be system

data.question: What is a requirement?
data.b: A statement of what the system must do or what characteristics it needs to have

data.question: Which type of requirement describes what the software should do?
data.b: User requirements

data.question: What is requirements elicitation?
data.b: Testing the system
data.c: Researching and discovering requirements from users, customers, and stakeholders

data.question: What is the primary reason the as-is step might be skipped during analysis?
data.b: When there is no current system or it is irrelevant
data.d: When the project is over budget

data.question: Which type of requirement defines the characteristics the system should have?
data.b: User requirements

data.question: What type of requirement focuses on what the business needs?
data.b: User requirements

data.question: Which type of interview seeks a broad and roughly defined set of information?
data.b: Structured interview

data.question: Which requirements analysis strategy involves examining the time taken for processes?
data.b: Duration analysis

data.question: What is a use case?
data.b: A representation of how a system interacts with its environment

data.question: What is the goal of creating use cases?
data.b: To describe all tasks users need to perform

data.question: What is an actor in use case analysis?
data.b: Any entity that interacts with the system

data.question: What is a process model?
data.a: A graphical way of representing how a business system operates
data.b: A type of hardware

data.question: What does DFD stand for?
data.b: Digital Function Display

data.question: What is the purpose of balancing in Data Flow Diagrams (DFDs)?
data.a: To ensure external entities are connected properly
data.b: To guarantee all processes have at least two outputs
data.c: To ensure consistency between levels, so data flows and data stores at boundaries match
data.d: To create a visual representation of logic within processes

data.question: Which DFD level shows the major high-level processes, data stores, and external entities?
data.b: Level 0 diagram

data.question: Which modeling technique is best used when process logic is complex and relies on rules linking conditions with actions?
data.b: Structured English

data.question: According to basic DFD rules, which of the following is correct regarding data stores?
data.a: They must be connected to external entities.
data.b: They can be connected to other data stores directly.
data.c: They must receive at least two input data flows.
data.d: They should be connected to at least one process.

data.question: Does a Data Flow Diagram (DFD) show the internal logic inside processes?
data.a: Yes, it is the primary purpose of a DFD.
data.b: Yes, but only in Level 2 diagrams.
data.c: No, DFDs do not show logic inside processes.
data.d: No, unless decision trees are explicitly drawn inside them.

data.question: How many context diagrams does a process model have?
data.b: One

data.question: What is a Level 0 DFD?
data.b: A diagram that shows all internal processes at the first level of numbering
data.c: A diagram that decomposes a single process
data.d: A diagram with no data stores

data.question: What does it mean for DFDs to be balanced?
data.a: They all have the same number of processes
data.b: The Level 0 and Level 1 DFDs show the same data stores and data flows at the boundaries
data.d: They all have the same number of symbols

data.question: What is Structured English used for?
data.b: To describe the work that a process performs using short sentences

data.question: Which of the following are correct about DFDs? i. A DFD must have at least one process ii. A process must have only inputs and no outputs iii. A process must have at least one input and one output data flow iv. Data stores must be connected to at least one process v. External entities must be connected to each other directly
data.b: i, iii and iv

data.question: What is a data model?
data.a: A formal way of representing data used and created by a business system
data.b: A type of hardware

data.question: What are the three basic elements of an ERD?
data.b: Entities, attributes, relationships

data.question: What is an identifier?
data.a: An attribute that cannot be unique
data.b: The attribute that can uniquely identify one instance of an entity

data.question: What does 1:1 cardinality mean?
data.a: One parent associated with many children
data.b: One parent associated with one child
data.c: Many parents associated with many children

data.question: What is normalization?
data.a: A technique to make models more complex
data.b: A technique applying rules to validate a model and eliminate redundancy

data.question: Which of the following are correct about cardinality? i. 1:1 means one entity associated with one other ii. 1:N means one entity associated with many others iii. M:N means many entities associated with many others iv. 1:1 is the most common cardinality v. 1:N is the most common cardinality
data.b: i, ii and v

data.question: Which of the following are correct about modality? i. Modality indicates optional or mandatory ii. Null means optional iii. Not null means mandatory iv. Modality is shown with zero or bar v. Modality is the same as cardinality
data.b: i, ii and iv

data.question: Which of the following are correct about relationships? i. Relationships are associations between entities ii. Relationships are shown lines iii. Relationships have cardinality iv. Relationships have modality v. Relationships are rectangles
data.b: i, ii and iv

data.question: Which of the following are correct about data models? i. Logical model shows logical organization ii. Logical model shows implementation details iii. Physical model shows how data will be stored iv. Logical models drawn during analysis v. Physical models drawn during analysis
data.b: i, iii and iv

data.question: Which of the following are correct about normalization? i. Normalization eliminates redundant data ii. Normalization prevents update anomalies iii. Normalization makes data models unstable iv. Normalization uses a series of rules v. Normalization is optional
data.b: i, iii and v

data.question: What is the primary difference between a logical data model and a physical data model?
data.a: A logical data model shows storage details, while a physical model is used only during analysis
data.b: A logical data model shows logical organization during analysis, while a physical model shows storage details during design
data.c: A logical data model eliminates redundancy, while a physical model focuses on cardinality
data.d: A logical data model represents relationships, while a physical model represents entities

data.question: What is the primary purpose of a data dictionary in systems analysis?
data.a: To physically store the application's user data securely
data.b: To define or look up metadata about entities, attributes, and relationships
data.c: To provide a graphic representation of hardware components
data.d: To act as middleware between client and server architectures

data.question: In an Entity Relationship Diagram (ERD), how are the basic elements typically represented?
data.a: Entities as circles, Attributes as lines, Relationships as squares
data.b: Entities as rectangles, Attributes as information about entities, Relationships as lines
data.c: Entities as lines, Attributes as rectangles, Relationships as circles
data.d: Entities as triangles, Attributes as data points, Relationships as arrows

data.question: Which system acquisition strategy involves using an Application Service Provider (ASP) or Software as a Service (SaaS)?
data.b: Packaged software

data.question: Which of the following best describes the goal of normalization in data modeling?
data.a: To balance processing loads between clients and servers
data.b: To translate between different vendors' software
data.c: To ensure that all relationships are mandatory
data.d: To validate data models, eliminate redundancy, and prevent update anomalies

data.question: What is interface design?
data.b: Defining how the system interacts with external entities

data.question: How many principles guide user interface design?
data.b: Five

data.question: What is arguably the most important interface design principle?
data.b: Consistency

data.question: What is the first step in the user interface design process?
data.b: Develop use scenarios

data.question: What is an Interface Structure Diagram (ISD)?
data.b: Diagram showing all interfaces and connections

data.question: In a client-server architecture, what defines a 'Thick Client'?
data.a: A client that performs only presentation logic
data.b: A client where a small portion of application logic resides
data.c: A client where most of the application logic resides
data.d: A client that exclusively handles data storage

data.question: What is the primary function of middleware in a system architecture?
data.a: To translate between products from different vendors
data.b: To replace the need for client-server architectures
data.c: To handle presentation logic for the user interface
data.d: To store master and transaction files permanently

data.question: Which of the following is considered a nonfunctional requirement regarding performance?
data.b: Response time and update latency

data.question: According to the summary, which database type is predominantly used for data warehousing with pre-aggregated measures?
data.b: Object

data.question: Which type of file contains past transactions for reference rather than for active processing?
data.b: Audit file

data.question: What is the implementation phase?
data.b: Coding, testing, and deploying the system

data.question: What is a test plan?
data.b: A document specifying test objectives, test cases, and expected results

data.question: What is user acceptance testing (UAT)?
data.b: Testing done by end users to verify the system meets their needs

data.question: What is direct conversion?
data.a: Running old and new systems simultaneously
data.b: Instant cutover where the old system is stopped and new system started
data.c: Converting one location at a time
data.d: Converting one module at a time

data.question: What is the three-step model of organizational change?
data.b: Unfreeze, change, refreeze

data.question: What do object-oriented systems view an information system as?
data.b: A collection of self-contained objects

data.question: What is a class in OO concepts?
data.b: A template defining shared attributes and methods

data.question: What OO development principle states that an object exposes only its interface while keeping its internal implementation private?
data.b: Encapsulation

data.question: Which UML diagram is a static model showing classes, attributes, operations, and relationships?
data.b: Class diagram

data.question: Which of the following allows subclasses to inherit attributes and methods from superclasses?
data.b: Message passing

data.question: What is an object in OO concepts?
data.b: A specific instance of a class

data.question: What is a method in OO concepts?
data.b: An action an object can perform

data.question: What is encapsulation?
data.b: Combining data and processes into a single entity

data.question: What is information hiding?
data.a: Allowing other objects to see internal implementation
data.b: Other objects see only the interface, not internal implementation

data.question: What is inheritance?
data.a: Subclasses have no relation to superclass
data.b: Subclasses inherit all attributes and methods from superclass

data.question: Which conversion strategy involves running the old and new systems simultaneously?
data.b: Parallel conversion

data.question: What is the primary purpose of a post-implementation review?
data.a: To plan the initial budget for the project
data.b: To evaluate the system's success by comparing actual performance against expected benefits
data.c: To design the user interface of the new system
data.d: To gather requirements from the stakeholders

data.question: Which conversion location strategy involves rolling out the new system gradually location?
data.b: Direct conversion

data.question: In the context of system migration, what does a modular conversion entail?
data.a: Converting the entire system at once
data.b: Converting the system one module at a time
data.c: Running the old and new systems in parallel
data.d: Testing the system at a single location before a full rollout

data.question: What does capacity planning in the maintenance phase primarily address?
data.b: Planning for future growth and system resources

data.question: What is an advantage of direct conversion?
data.b: Fast and cheap

data.question: What is a disadvantage of direct conversion?
data.b: Any undiscovered bug immediately disrupts operations

data.question: What is parallel conversion?
data.b: Running old and new systems simultaneously, comparing outputs

data.question: What is an advantage of parallel conversion?
data.b: Low risk (old system available if problems occur)

data.question: Why did the object-oriented approach to system development evolve?
data.b: Because developer time now dominates costs, and OO emphasizes reuse and modularity
data.c: Because users demanded faster processing speeds

data.question: What is the primary analysis and communication tool in OO development?
data.b: State machine models

data.question: What is the purpose of the 'Unfreeze' step in the three-step model of organizational change?
data.b: To implement the new system
data.c: To stop all business operations immediately
data.d: To loosen attachment to the old system

data.question: What is the function of a 'Migration Plan' in system implementation?
data.a: To plan for transitioning from the old system to the new system
data.b: To physically move servers to a new location
data.c: To upgrade employee software skills without changing systems

data.question: Which of the following is true about polymorphism based on the glossary?
data.a: It means the same interface is used for different types
data.b: It completely hides all class methods
data.c: It forces subclasses to delete superclass attributes

data.question: What are the core Object-Oriented Principles according to the text?
data.a: Use-case driven, Architecture-centric, Iterative and incremental
data.b: Data-driven, Design-centric, Waterfall

data.question: Which of the following best defines a 'Class' in Object-Oriented programming?
data.b: A template for objects
data.d: A combination of data and processes

data.question: What does an 'Object' represent in the context of Object-Oriented programming?
data.b: An instance of a class

data.question: How is a 'Method' defined in Object-Oriented terminology?
data.b: Data and processes combined together
data.c: An action that an object performs
data.d: The visible interface of a class

data.question: Which term describes the concept of keeping data and processes together?
data.b: Information Hiding

data.question: What happens in the process of Inheritance?
data.a: An object performs a specific action
data.b: A subclass inherits from a superclass
data.c: Data and processes are hidden from the user
data.d: Only the interface is made visible

data.question: What does Information Hiding refer to in Object-Oriented design?
data.b: Data and processes are grouped together
data.c: A subclass inherits from a superclass
data.d: Templates for objects are kept secret

data.question: According to the provided text, which of the following is NOT one of the main OO Principles?
data.b: Architecture-centric

data.question: If you are working with a specific instance of a class, what are you working with?
data.b: A method

data.question: When only the interface is visible and the underlying implementation is concealed, this demonstrates:
data.b: Information Hiding
